questions.q: '___ European union' — a or an, and why?
questions.a: 'a' — 'European' starts with a yoo- consonant SOUND. A wrong answer 'an' reveals letter-matching instead of sound-matching.

questions.q: 'He has ___ friends, so he feels lonely.' few or a few?
questions.a: 'few' — 'lonely' signals the negative reading (almost none). A wrong answer 'a few' misses that the 'a' flips scarcity to sufficiency — attitude, not style.

questions.q: Fix: 'Less students attended the match today.'
questions.a: 'Fewer students' — countables take fewer; 'less' is for mass nouns. A wrong answer accepting 'less' shows the count/mass partition isn't built.

questions.q: The board determiner set: a/an/the/zero by the specificity algorithm; a-vs-an by SOUND; the few/little attitude pair (few=almost none, a few=some); count-mass pairing (few/many vs little/much, fewer vs less); and fixed patterns (the+superlative, zero article for ______).
